newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 14.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Sydney Swans beat Essendon at the Sydney Football Ground yesterday to move into seventh spot on the Australian Football League ladder. The Swans trailed by 20 points with 10 minutes to go in the fourth quarter before making their comeback. Page 25.

Australian tennis player Rachel McQuillan was defeated 6-1, 6-3 by Spain's No.2 ranked player Maria Luisa Serna in her Federation Cup match yesterday. Earlier, Arantxa Sanchez Vicario beat Annabel Ellwood 6-2, 6-0 in 57 minutes. Spain won the tie 3-2. Page 26.

Australian sailer Brett Crowther is creating one of the largest and most radical racing sailboats the world has seen for a 30,000 nautical mile race starting in France on December 31 2000 that involves the 10 fastest yachts in the world. Page 26.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian Rugby Union team defeated England 25-6 in their international Cook Cup match at the Sydney Football Stadium on Saturday night in front of a 40,000-strong crowd. Winger Ben Tune starred for Australia with two tries. Page 26.

Australian golfer Karrie Webb has an outside chance of victory in the US Women's Open after moving within seven strokes of leader Alison Nicholas. Webb shot a six-under-par third round of 65. Page 27.

The Australian cricket team reached 9-278 in their one-day match against Scotland on Saturday. Batsman Michael Slater led the way for Australia with 95 runs, but Scotland could only manage 6-95 in 21.5 overs before rain washed out play. Page 30.
THE AGE

Australian cyclist Stuart O'Grady yesterday was in fifth place overall in the Tour de France after the 194-kilometre seventh stage from Marennes to Bordeaux. O'Grady finished 21st with his French team GAN continuing to dominate the race. Page D2.

The Australian under-20 women's basketball team will play in the final of the under-20 world championship after defeating host nation Brazil 71-60. Australia dominated in the final minutes to win the game in front of a crowd of more than 15,000. Page D8.

The Australian Football League is expected to investigate an incident during the Richmond-Hawthorn match yesterday involving Richmond coach Robert Walls. Walls and his assistant Jeff Geischen became involved in an on-field fight at half time, pulling players out of a skirmish. Page D3
THE HERALD SUN

Holden racing driver Greg Murphy won two of three 17-lap races at the penultimate round of the Australian Shell Touring Car Series at Mallala, near Adelaide, yesterday. After the race Murphy said he would prefer Ford drivers Glenn Seton or John Bowe to win the championship rather than fellow Holden driver Russell Ingall. Page 86.

The International Federation of Netball Associations has approved the introduction of player payments, giving a boost to Australia's most popular women's sport. Australia and New Zealand have long been campaigners for the sport to turn professional. Page 1.

Queensland runner Pat Carroll won his fourth Gold Coast Marathon yesterday after passing South African Gert Thys in the final 200 metres. Canberra-based Olympic runner Susan Hobson won the women's event. Page 81.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Australian diving team to compete in the World Diving Cup in Mexico in September was announced yesterday. The team, which manager Rob Crick describes as a blend of youth and experience, was announced after national selection trials in Brisbane. Page 3.

The Australian youth soccer team defeated South Africa 2-0 in their soccer international at the Bruce Athletics Field in Canberra on Saturday night. Australia had a win and a draw against South Africa when the teams met in South Africa last year. Page 31.

The Australian softball team will play world champion the United States in the final of the Superball international women's softball tournament. Australia beat Japan 6-2 to ensure the finals berth, and has a tournament record of four wins and one loss. Page 4.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
